The generalised ordered logit

Source: R/gol.R
gologt.Rd

An ordered outcome (a risk level, a charge's seriousness, a sentence band) regressed on covariates without forcing each covariate to act the same way at every cut of the scale. For an outcome with levels 1, ..., M, each threshold j < M has its own intercept and slopes, P(y > j) = F(a_j + x b_j) with F the logistic distribution function (Peterson and Harrell 1990; Williams 2006, the parameterisation of 'gologit2'); a covariate named in par keeps one slope for all the thresholds, as in the proportional-odds model, so that par = x is that model. O'Connell and Laniyonu (2025) find racial disparity in a risk tool concentrated at the low-to-medium cut and absent at the medium-to-high one, which a proportional-odds fit averages away.

Usage

gologt(data, y, x, par = NULL, lev = NULL, level = 0.95, maxit = 500)

# S3 method for class 'gologt'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit.

y

The name of the ordered outcome column: an ordered factor or a factor (its levels in order), numbers (in increasing order) or text (with lev).

x

The names of the covariate columns: numeric or logical, at least one.

par

NULL, or the names of covariates in x held parallel (one slope for every threshold).

lev

NULL, or the levels of the outcome from lowest to highest, each present in the data; needed for text.

level

The confidence level of the Wald intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

maxit

The quasi-Newton steps: one whole number from 1.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class gologt, a list: coef, one row per parameter (term, thr the threshold, as "low|med", or "all" for a parallel slope; est, se, z, p, lo, hi); wald, one row per covariate (term, stat, df, p; NA for a parallel one); lr, the test against proportional odds (stat, df, p; NA when every slope is parallel); fit (loglik, aic, iter, conv, 1 when converged); vcov; lev; and n.

Details

The parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood (quasi-Newton steps with the analytic gradient, in the compiled core), with standard errors from the inverse of the Hessian. A free covariate's slopes may cross, so that a category's fitted probability is negative for some x; the fit refuses such points within the data. wald tests, for each free covariate, that its slopes are equal at every threshold (the test 'gologit2' uses to choose the parallel ones), and lr is the likelihood-ratio test of the fit against the proportional-odds model.

References

Peterson, B. and Harrell, F. E. (1990). Partial proportional odds models for ordinal response variables. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C, 39(2), 205-217. doi:10.2307/2347760

Williams, R. (2006). Generalized ordered logit/partial proportional odds models for ordinal dependent variables. The Stata Journal, 6(1), 58-82. doi:10.1177/1536867X0600600104

O'Connell, M. and Laniyonu, A. (2025). Threshold-specific cumulative-logit models for actuarial-risk audit. Race and Justice, 15(3), 428-453.

See also

gocoef() for the slopes by threshold.

Examples

set.seed(7)
n <- 400
d <- data.frame(race = rbinom(n, 1, 0.4), age = rnorm(n))
e1 <- 0.5 + 0.8 * d$race - 0.5 * d$age
e2 <- -1 + 0.1 * d$race - 0.5 * d$age
u <- runif(n)
d$risk <- factor(1 + (u < plogis(e1)) + (u < plogis(e2)), 1:3,
                 c("low", "med", "high"))
r <- gologt(d, "risk", c("race", "age"), par = "age")
r
#> gologt: generalised ordered logit, 400 rows, 3 levels; log-likelihood -414.564
#>         term      thr        est         se          z            p         lo
#>  (Intercept)  low|med  0.5549532 0.14198273  3.9085966 9.283381e-05  0.2766722
#>  (Intercept) med|high -0.8280251 0.14776492 -5.6036652 2.098659e-08 -1.1176390
#>         race  low|med  0.5972905 0.22943154  2.6033496 9.231777e-03  0.1476129
#>         race med|high -0.1312269 0.22560745 -0.5816604 5.607954e-01 -0.5734094
#>          age      all -0.5709891 0.09757872 -5.8515741 4.869423e-09 -0.7622399
#>          hi
#>   0.8332342
#>  -0.5384112
#>   1.0469681
#>   0.3109556
#>  -0.3797383
